anchor.quote: Let $f$ be the parameter of a call
Here $m$ is the factor by which the parameter grows
Let $s$ be the number of subcalls of one call.
Let $\Phi(f)$ be the cost of a call divided by the volume $V$ it works on.
Let $C$ be a constant such that the call's own outside work is at most $C(mf)^\lambda$

anchor.note: Big-O notation, covered by the undergraduate asymptotic analysis background.

anchor.quote: Here $\Omega$ is the bit count of one axis chunk
Let $\nu$ count the levels of unrolling

gaps.note: Contradicts the page's own statement that the construction gives $s<Wm$ (so $s/W<m$). Only $s/W<m$ makes $\log_m(s/W)<1$, so a $\lambda<1$ with $\lambda>\log_m(s/W)$ exists, and the worked example ($s/W=3/2<m=2$) also has $s/W<m$. It should read $s/W<m$. The citation also gives no account of why.

gaps.quote: so the internal sum is at most a constant times $f^\lambda$ for every $\lambda>0$.
gaps.note: Overstated. The geometric sum converges only when the ratio $(s/W)/m^\lambda$ is below 1, i.e. $\lambda>\log_m(s/W)$ (and $\lambda<1$); for smaller $\lambda$ the ratio is at least 1 and the sum is not bounded by a constant. Correct: for every $\lambda$ with $\log_m(s/W)<\lambda<1$.

gaps.term: choice of lambda misses outside-work condition
gaps.quote: Taking $\lambda$ with $\log_m(s/W)<\lambda<1$ makes the ratio below 1
gaps.note: The outside-work bound $C(mf)^\lambda$ was only shown to hold when $\lambda>\tau(1+\eta/\vartheta)$, yet the final choice of $\lambda$ ignores it. A valid $\lambda$ must exceed both $\log_m(s/W)$ and $\tau(1+\eta/\vartheta)$ and be below 1, which needs the missing hypothesis $\tau(1+\eta/\vartheta)<1$ (small enough $\eta$); $\tau<1$ alone does not give it.

gaps.quote: and the leaves cost $O(f^\sigma d^{\vartheta(1-\sigma)})\le O(f^\lambda)$.
gaps.note: The last inequality is not justified. The page only gives $f\ge d^\vartheta$ at internal nodes, which yields $d^{\vartheta(1-\sigma)}\le f^{1-\sigma}$ and so only $O(f)$. To reach $O(f^\lambda)$ one needs $d^{\vartheta(1-\sigma)}\le f^{\lambda-\sigma}$, i.e. $f\ge d^{\vartheta(1-\sigma)/(\lambda-\sigma)}$, or $d$ treated as a constant factor; neither is stated.

$u$ was the bit width of an address field (earlier page and earlier in this page, $u=f\Omega$ bits), but here it is the number of chunks at a leaf; the page does not announce the change. The leaf cost $O((s/W)^\nu u)$ also assumes a per-chunk kernel cost per unit volume that is never stated.

gaps.quote: Each leaf is handled by one kernel per chunk, at cost $O(f/m^\nu)$.
gaps.note: "Kernel" is never defined or linked, and the claim that a leaf costs $O(f/m^\nu)$ (per unit volume) is asserted without saying what the kernel does or why it is linear in the number of chunks.

gaps.quote: A row addition on fields of $u=f\Omega$ bits costs $O(V(u^\tau+1))$.
gaps.note: The page cites only the cost of an address interchange, $O(Vu^\tau)$, and then asserts the cost of a row addition without saying how a row addition is carried out with interchanges or why it adds only $O(V)$.
